title: across-refs reports a genuine id collision as one task with disagreeing states
description:
Found while building the Quest board mod (QCLI-431), whose pane creates tasks.

quest task create takes the next id from the working tree plus every LOCAL ref (QCLI-279/290), so a record that is written but not yet committed in ANOTHER checkout of the same repository is invisible to it. Reproduced during QCLI-431 with two worktrees of one repository: a create on main left uncommitted, then a create on feat/other, and both minted T-1. Committing the first closed the window and the next create minted T-2. ODOC-379 was minted this way on 2026-10-02 -- the operator test record from the prototype New task box, created in opum-doc checkout while a branch held the same id, and the fleet sweep tracker read failed on it.

The allocator half cannot be closed from inside the process: it cannot see another worktree uncommitted files, and it deliberately never fetches. Detection can be closed, and is not.

quest task list --across-refs treats the same id on two refs as two STATES of one task and picks no winner. That is right for the shape it was built for -- one task whose status differs across refs -- and silently wrong for a genuine collision, where two distinct records share an id. The read then reports a single task whose states disagree, and the fact that there are two different records never surfaces.

QCLI-431 carries the pane-side half only: the board draws an unlanded record as the collision window it is, so the person can land it. Detection belongs here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task list --across-refs distinguishes a genuine collision -- the same id on two refs naming records that are not the same task -- from one task whose states disagree across refs, and reports the former rather than folding it into the latter.

The discriminator it uses is stated in the record and is defensible from the data a task record actually carries; a pair it cannot tell apart is reported as an unresolved collision rather than assumed to be one task.

A test reproduces the QCLI-431 shape -- two refs carrying the same id for two different tasks -- and asserts the collision is reported, alongside a test that the legitimate same-task-different-states read is unchanged.
The behaviour is recorded in the --across-refs guide and in the task-creation guide section on refs-aware allocation.
